doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Jackie Gleason's theme and playing trumpet with Palmer
summary: Palmer recalls Sammy Spear and Ray Block, then the comedy routine in Newark where Gleason played I Love You Truly.

blocks.x: Now before we quit we’ve got to talk about The Jackie Gleason Show a little bit.
And Ray Block. Sammy and I were great friends anyway so.
How did that theme song go? The Jackie Gleason theme song?
Gee what was it. I forgot what it was.

Well Gleason had a good ear for music. And of course when he was big enough to have writers, he would think of something, he would hum something, maybe a couple of bars. [humms] and they would have to write a whole thing on it, you know, but with that as the theme. But he was very musical, Gleason. In Newark, when we were in Newark, he wanted, he loved to play the trumpet you know, but he couldn’t do it. He could blow good, he had natural chops. So I went with him in Newark. He says, “Let’s go into town, I’ve got to buy a horn.” So we went and I picked out a horn — fifteen dollars. Then he drove everybody crazy at the place. Then he used to call me out. He used to be on the floor and he’d say, “Come on out and we’ll play,” because I showed him how to play “I Love You Truly,” which was first valve and open, it was easy, just eight bars. And he called me out on the floor and he’d take the trumpet and make a big deal about wiping his lips and chops and putting them together and that. And so then he played the first eight bars, which is all he knew, and I’d play the harmony to it.
So it made him sound almost like he could play, right?

Yeah. After eight bars then he says, “Well now we go for the big one,” and he wipes his lip and everything, then he goes powwww, and then I’d top him, then he’d try to go higher, and I’d top him and then he’d go higher, ‘till finally he says, “This last note is the one I grab toilet paper on” something to that effect you know. “This last note is where I go and get the bathroom paper out,” and he’d make a big thing on that.
Yeah, it wasn’t even a note.
No, no. But he had natural good chops, he did have.
